title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.23206v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit request for the underlying harmful objective. We identify this \textbf{scene-state safety vulnerability} and introduce \textbf{SceneSafetyBench}, comprising 375 image--question pairs spanning Initial, Medium, and Ultimate scene states and five visual presentations. Across eight VLMs, scene-state inputs elicit harmful assistance with attack success rates (ASRs) of 45.6--72.3\%. Comparative analysis across three VLMs shows that scene-state inputs most closely resemble QR-related images in their layer-wise safety-related signal profiles, while exhibiting lower average late-layer readouts and distinct signal dynamics during generation. translated_title: 读取场景状态：揭示视觉-语言模型中的安全失效
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言模型（VLM）可以通过解读视觉事件来提供有害协助，即使没有对潜在有害目标的明确请求。我们识别了这种“场景状态安全漏洞”，并引入了SceneSafetyBench基准，其中包含375个图像-问题对，涵盖初始、中期和最终三种场景状态以及五种视觉呈现方式。在八个VLM上的实验表明，场景状态输入能够以45.6%至72.3%的攻击成功率（ASR）诱发有害协助。对三个VLM的比较分析显示，场景状态输入在其逐层安全相关信号特征上与二维码相关图像最为相似，同时表现出较低的平均后期层读数以及生成过程中独特的信号动态。为了将这一漏洞转化为系统性攻击，我们提出了S3TA方法，它将有害目标转化为场景状态，独立查询图像-问题对，并将结果组装成有害协助。
tldr: 该论文发现了视觉-语言模型的“场景状态安全漏洞”——即使没有明确有害请求，模型解读场景状态图像也会提供有害协助（攻击成功率45.6%–72.3%），并提出了SceneSafetyBench基准和S3TA系统性攻击方法来揭示这一安全失效。
en_tdlr: The paper uncovers a "scene-state safety vulnerability" in vision-language models, where interpreting scene-state images elicits harmful assistance even without explicit harmful requests (45.6–72.3% ASR), and introduces the SceneSafetyBench benchmark along with the S3TA systematic attack method to expose these safety failures.
